symptom: `mxcli git note -p App.mpr --write | head -1` writes no mx_metadata note and says nothing: the pipeline exits with head's status 0 (141 under pipefail), `git notes --ref=mx_metadata show HEAD` reports no note; `| tail -1` and an unpiped run both write it
cause: `annotateCommits` printed each commit's note (one JSON line, ~660 KB on a whole-project commit) before writing it. A Go program writing to a stdout whose reader has gone is killed by SIGPIPE, so the first print to the closed pipe ended the process ahead of `writeNote` — for that commit and every later one
insight: Any print that precedes a side effect is a kill point once stdout is a pipe: Go dies on EPIPE to fd 1 unless SIGPIPE is notified or ignored, so ignoring Fprintf's error changes nothing. Do every write first and report afterwards; a preview with no side effect can stream. The issue's own suggestion (write then print, per commit) is not enough with two commits — the second print still kills before the second write, and a two-arm control showed exactly that (HEAD~1 written, HEAD lost). That same arm explains the upstream "verified fixed on main" comment: it reported exit 141 on both builds and 1 note for a repository two commits ahead, which is the race landing differently, not a fix — `annotateCommits` was unchanged on that commit. Test with a pipe whose read end is closed before the child starts: `| head -1` with the race taken out, so a small fixture note is enough; assert the child ended on SIGPIPE as the control that the scenario fired
test: `cmd/mxcli/gitnote_sigpipe_test.go` (`TestGitNote_WriteSurvivesAClosedStdout`, real main() in a child via TestRunMainHelper)
